newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia and South Korea sign investment pact.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia and South Korea sign investment pact.

text.p: Cambodia and South Korea on Monday signed investment and technical cooperation accords which are expected to strengthen business ties, officials said.

"The two agreements (we) have signed are marking another milestone in the chapter of Cambodian-Korean relations," said K.T. Park, head of South Korea's diplomatic mission in Cambodia, at a signing ceremony at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Officials said an investment protection and promotion agreement would protect Korean companies against any possible nationalisation of industry and establish most favoured nation trade preferences between the two countries.
An economic, scientific and technical agreement would promote the exchange of experts, information and equipment from various fields, said Park.
He said the accords fostered closer relations and increased investment between the two countries.
But Park added "there is still one important task to be realised", a reference to the fact South Korea has yet to establish full diplomatic relations with Cambodia.
Seoul established mission-level ties in Phnom Penh last May after 21 years of diplomatic absence, but because of opposition by King Norodom Sihanouk, ties have not been further formalised.

Sihanouk has a house in North Korea and was a close friend of the Stalinist state's late leader, Kim Il-sung, a relationship he has often cited as the reason for his opposition to full ties with Seoul.
South Korean firms invested $12 million in Cambodia last year, mainly in garments, said Park.
Seoul opened a trade office in Cambodia last October.
